systemicObservation: Fifth consecutive candidate with no blocker, and the single surviving SHOULD-FIX is narrower than any predecessor's. It is also a new failure mode worth naming, because it is the opposite of the enumeration drift that dominated v5 through v8. There the problem was a list that failed to grow when a member was added; here a list was edited by substitution - the platform targets took the offline-closure property's place in the named-property set rather than joining it - so the set stayed the same size while its coverage moved. A grep for 'which clauses enumerate this set' would have found governingSources[3].role and reported it current, because it does name three properties; only a diff against the predecessor shows one was swapped out, and only a search for who still relies on the removed member shows the cost. The check this chain has not yet institutionalised is the removal check: when a repair edits a list, diff the list against the predecessor and, for anything dropped, grep the artifact for clauses that still depend on it. Run against v10 that check yields exactly V10-S1. The substantive contract is now unchanged for five generations - v10 touched no selector rule, no G16 class and no identity dependency - and what remains is provenance recording.
verdictBasis: Zero blockers and one SHOULD-FIX; the dispatch admits ACCEPT only at zero and zero. All four claimed repairs are real and verified against the subject's bytes and against the live D-002 entry, and every predecessor verdict record is certified directly against frozen bytes. The surviving finding is a provenance defect with the underlying property independently confirmed true, not an under-selection escape.
verdictStatement: v10 repairs the D-002 platform vocabulary exactly against the governing bytes - four OS/architecture targets matching the adopted Platforms sentence member for member, with OS-only tokens explicitly invalid and the sentence quoted in the LIVE block - which closes the v9 blocker-adjacent finding at its root rather than at its symptom. ROLELESS-NA cells are now qualification-neutral against the DR-118 language gates in two agreeing clauses, neither omitted nor auto-failed. The live-pin locator design holds, the prior LIVE block is correctly demoted under the method's standing rule, and the roster is closed at zero off-roster paths with the selector, the G16 classes and the identity dependencies all byte-identical. One finding survives, and it is a swap rather than an omission: the inherited pin's named-property list gained the four platform targets by losing 'authoritative offline closure out of slice 1', and the LIVE block re-verifies only what replaced it - while SL-5's note, ID-DEP-C4 and whatThisDoesNotDo all still rest on the property that was dropped. The property is true; this reviewer confirmed it live. What is missing is the artifact's stated warrant for continuing to rely on it, which is the same gap this reviewer raised at v9 and which the repair narrowed rather than closed. DR-121 remains OPEN; DR-G16 remains PROPOSED, not QUALIFIED.
authorityOfThisVerdict: This verdict is a reviewer opinion recorded for coordinator disposition. It applies nothing, edits no subject, does not mark DR-121 SATISFIED, marks no gate QUALIFIED, authorizes no implementation, chooses no CI vendor, mints no D-096 (A) grant, and does not touch docs/v2/architecture/08-decision-and-readiness-register.md or docs/coop/COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md. It did not edit the review prompt it was given.
coordinatorNote: A v11 needs no new roster paths for the SHOULD-FIX: /recordedInputs and /reMeasurementAtV10 both carried this cycle's edits and both are where V10-S1's repair lands. No design decision is outstanding - all four D-002 properties are confirmed live at 7da75955…, so restoring the list and extending the re-verification is a recording edit. The advisories add /g16Tests/corpus/fixtureDomainBasis (already rostered) and /selector/algorithm (not rostered since v9) if the coordinator wants them folded. One scoping question is worth putting to the coordinator rather than the author: whether deferred-slot values are platform tokens subject to the new validation rule, which decides whether DEF-WIN should become two arch-qualified slots before Windows enters. Two process notes. First, the frozen-predecessor-readable convention has now paid off in six consecutive cycles and let this verdict certify all eleven predecessor records. Second, V10-S1 is the first finding in this chain produced by substitution inside a list rather than by failure to extend one; adding a removal check to the authoring pass - diff each edited list against the predecessor, and for anything dropped grep for clauses that still depend on it - would close the class.
